items.note: Aran Islands, Galway Bay, north light (Eeragh). Not Arranmore in Donegal, and not Arran in Scotland.
'Daily' is an OCR misreading of 'Baily'. The station list prints 'Howth Baily'.

Mew Island is where the Copeland light stands. The example ('Terns breed on Mew Island') may be the keeper's remark naming the island, not a station heading. Either way it points to the Copeland station.
Oyster Island had north and south lights, but the station file has a single entry, which already includes 'Oyster Island N.'.
Rathlin Island, Antrim: the only Rathlin station that isn't Rathlin O'Birne.

Uncertain. The words name the South Maiden tower, but maidens-south is only 'seen' in 1887. The 1881 list prints just 'Maidens', which is under maidens-north. If the 1881 'Maidens' return came from the south tower, maidens-south is right. If 'South Maiden lighthouse' is only mentioned in a Maidens North remark, use maidens-north.

notes: Things to check: (1) n=1154 'South Maiden lighthouse', 1881: find out which Maidens tower sent the 1881 return. The station file lists maidens-south only for 1887, and the 1881 'Maidens' entry sits under maidens-north. (2) n=846 'Mew Island': check whether it is an observation heading or just part of a remark ('Terns breed on Mew Island') inside the Copeland entry. (3) Oyster Island has one entry in the station file even though it had two lights (N/S). If the reports ever separate them, the file may need an oyster-island-south. (4) The Arran items with a line break inside ('Arran Island\nNorth/South', 'Rathlin\nIsland') are the same stations as the one-line forms. Only the extraction differs.
